visual.general_description: Photograph of a printed OCT report of both eyes with colour retinal thickness maps, a thickness table, two macular grids and two cross-sectional scans.
visual.detailed_description: Photograph of a paper OCT printout with the header "Eye: Both". Upper half: four colour retinal-thickness maps in two pairs (Retina thickness and Inner Retinal thickness). The left pair shows a mostly green map with a small blue foveal centre; the right pair shows a map with a large pale/white-red central region and grey patches, and a red-orange thickness scale up to 750 on its colour bar. Between them are two circular macular grids and a table headed "ILM - OS/RPE measurements" with columns R, L and Diff (R-L). Printed values: Minimum in Fovea [μm] R 199, L 473, Diff -274; Central sector [μm] R 246, L 629, Diff -383; Area thickness [μm] R 286, L 411, Diff -125; Volume [mm3] R 8.08, L 11.61, Diff -3.53. The grid under the left maps has a central value of 246 and the grid under the right maps has a central value of 629. Lower half: two B-scans. The left scan shows a normal-appearing foveal depression; the right scan shows a dome-shaped elevation of the retinal layers at the macula with a darker region beneath it and a 200 μm scale bar. Header text with scan date and a name field is printed at the top, and device text at the bottom.

evidence.quote: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) confirmed increased central macular thickness, subretinal exudation, and vitreoretinal interface irregularities, correlating with observed clinical findings of active vasculitis.

These findings were further supported by optical coherence tomography (OCT), which revealed increased central retinal thickness, disruption of the foveal contour, and subretinal exudates in the left eye (Fig. 1).

assignments.rationale: Single-case article; the narrative cites Fig. 1 for this patient's OCT findings and the caption describes the same OCT.

evidence.quote: Widefield fundus photograph of the left eye showing venous tortuosity, vascular sheathing, and subretinal exudates characteristic of retinal vasculitis.

Peripheral vessel sheathing, which appeared as white cuff-like exudates surrounding the vessels on fundus examination, reflects perivascular infiltration by inflammatory cells and is considered a hallmark feature of RV^([]) (Fig. 2).

assignments.rationale: Single-case article; the caption describes the left eye fundus of this patient and the discussion cites Fig. 2 for fundus findings.
